title: PitchBook API Documentation
snippet:
##### **Step 1: Check out our test "Sandbox"**
To help developers get comfortable with the PitchBook API, a test "sandbox" environment has been created to show how API calls are structured and how to integrate them with your system. Please reach out to your account manager to request a sandbox key.

PitchBook will provide you with a unique API key that will allow you to make calls to the API. Your developer can use this key to retrieve our data and start powering your application. Your Customer Success Manager can help answer any questions about getting started with the API or the developer test "sandbox".
## Authentication
To authenticate to the PitchBook API, simply include a header named "Authorization" with the value of "PB-Token {API_KEY}" with each API request.
Replace {API_KEY} with your actual API key value.
In addition to an API key, please make sure you have purchased API credits. Each call has a defined cost. Reach out to your account manager to view and add credits to your API credit balance.
**Authentication Example**
> [https://api.pitchbook.com/{route}](https://api-v2.pitchbook.com/%7Broute%7D)
> Authorization: PB-Token LzUU9xgNjn7avDw5Bd96xNVS0t5dlGuD

title: PitchBook Python API Docs | dltHub
snippet:
PitchBook is a market intelligence platform providing a RESTful API for on-demand access to private and public market data such as companies, deals, investors, and funds. The REST API base URL is `https://api.pitchbook.com` and all requests require an Authorization header with a custom token format.

## How do I authenticate with the PitchBook API?
PitchBook authenticates requests using a static API key passed in the Authorization header with the format 'PB-Token {API_KEY}'.
**1. Get your credentials**
Access to the PitchBook API is a paid, contract-gated add-on and is not available via a self-serve dashboard. To obtain credentials: 1. Contact your PitchBook account manager or your organization's PitchBook administrator to request API access. 2. Once the add-on is enabled, your account manager will provision your API key. 3. Alternatively, you can log in to the PitchBook platform and navigate to 'My PitchBook' > 'Plugins & Apps' > 'PitchBook API' to reach out to the Direct Data team to initiate the request.
**2. Add them to `.dlt/secrets.toml`**
```
[sources.pitchbook_source]
api_key = "your_pb_token_here"
```
dlt reads this automatically at runtime — never hardcode tokens in your pipeline script. For production environments, see [setting up credentials with dlt](https://dlthub.com/docs/walkthroughs/add_credentials) for environment variable and vault-based options.

title: Help: PitchBook API - PitchBook
snippet:
**Accessing the API**
The PitchBook API is a RESTful implementation that most HTTP clients can easily access in your chosen language or via a web browser. Every call will use the same base URL: [https://api.pitchbook.com](https://api.pitchbook.com/)

**Create your API connection**
To start your API connection, you will need to send a request directly to our Direct Data team [through this link.](https://pitchbook.com/products/direct-access-data?utm_source=google&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=ROAST-Search-Brand-CentralEurope&adgroup=&utm_term=pitchbook&device=c&utm_content=&_bk=pitchbook&_bt=692687660336&_bm=e&_bn=g&_bg=159619233076&kwdaud=kwd-334479000139&sfid=-dc_pcrid_692687660336_pkw_pitchbook_pmt_e_slid__productid__pgrid_159619233076_ptaid_kwd-334479000139&gad_source=1&gbraid=0AAAAA9Xh_EaUNnreAs7FvuEymUQuWzBgU&gclid=CjwKCAjwktO_BhBrEiwAV70jXnWu1Xhd80_LMs-DIblUDGS_QRb1P1qKPKKGvKjtmcWtuiKdcPbrXxoC3ssQAvD_BwE)
Or if you’re a PitchBook client, you can also head to the Plugins & Apps section from the My PitchBook section of the left-hand sidebar on the PitchBook Platform and choose PitchBook API.

Our team will work with you to understand the insights and data you’re looking for and help you establish the API connection through an API key or authentication token. Available data for each entity type is packaged across several endpoints so you can map the data to your desired format and structure.

title: PitchBook integration
snippet:
PitchBook (a Morningstar company) is a market intelligence platform for private and public capital markets — companies, investors, funds, deals, people, limited partners, and service providers. Integrating PitchBook with Frontegg lets your application search and read this data on behalf of your users — all through Frontegg's integration layer (PitchBook Public API v2). PitchBook authenticates with a static API key sent on every request, so there is no OAuth flow.

PitchBook authenticates API requests with a static API key, sent on every request as the `Authorization: PB-Token <key>` header.
####
Step 1: Obtain your API key
PitchBook API keys are provisioned as part of a paid API add-on rather than generated self-serve. Contact your PitchBook account manager (or your organization's PitchBook administrator) to enable API access and issue an API key for your account.
PitchBook also offers a test **sandbox** environment that uses the same base URL with a separate key. If you want to try the integration before running against production data, ask your account manager for a sandbox key as well.
####
Keep your API key secure
The API key grants access to your PitchBook data through the API. Treat it like a password and never expose it in client-side code or commit it to version control. If it is exposed, ask PitchBook to rotate it.
###
Configure the Frontegg portal
Once you have your API key, configure the integration in the Frontegg portal:
1. Open the **Frontegg portal** and navigate to [ENVIRONMENT] → Integrations → PitchBook.
2. Paste your **API Key**.
3. Optionally set a **Default currency** — an ISO 4217 code (for example, `USD`, `EUR`, `GBP`, `JPY`) applied to all monetary fields in responses. Leave it blank to use PitchBook's default.
4. Click **Save**.
####
Keep your credentials secure
Never share or commit your API key to version control.

title: PitchBook connector
snippet:
Configure the PitchBook connector in [Control Center](https://app.writer.com/controlcenter) under **Integrations > Connectors**. The PitchBook connector uses API key authentication.
### Obtain a PitchBook API key
Create an API key in PitchBook:
1. Log in to your PitchBook account
2. Navigate to API settings or contact PitchBook support for API access
3. Generate a new API key
4. Copy the API key for use in Control Center
For detailed instructions, see [PitchBook’s API documentation](https://pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api).
### Configure the connector in Control Center
After obtaining your PitchBook API key:
1. Navigate to **Integrations > Connectors** in [Control Center](https://app.writer.com/controlcenter)
2. Select the PitchBook connector
3. Select who has access by default (all users or specific teams)
4. Select which tools to enable for your agents
5. Enter your PitchBook API key
